title: Pointwise standard tame charts for a generic torsor over a DVR
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring (a nonfield local principal ideal domain), $K$ a field with an $A$-algebra structure making it the fraction field of $A$, and $d:L	o\operatorname{Spec}A$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $b:\operatorname{Spec}K	o\operatorname{Spec}A$ for the algebra map, $L_K=L	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $j:L_K	o L$ for the first projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $G$ be a finite group with $|G|$ invertible in $A$ and $W	o L_K$ a finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $p:W	o L$ be its composite with $j$, and let $
u:p.\mathrm{normalization}	o L$ be the concrete relative normalization [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. If $
u$ is finite, every $x\in L$ has an affine etale neighbourhood $\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}R	o L$ and $y\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $\varphi(y)=x$, and integers $m\geq0$, $e_k>0$ for $k\in\operatorname{Fin}m$, all invertible in $R$, together with $f\in R$, such that $
u	imes_L\operatorname{Spec}R$ is isomorphic over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\prod_{k\in\operatorname{Fin}m}R[T]/(T^{e_k}-f)$. All schemes and rings lie in one universe; the group lies in the next universe. The case $m=0$ uses the empty product ring.

proof.text:
A DVR is Noetherian and regular. Smoothness makes L locally Noetherian and regular.
A uniformizer cuts out its closed fibre D as an effective Cartier divisor, since the
smooth morphism is flat. D is regular because it is smooth over the residue field.
The complement is the generic fibre. At a generic point of D its local ring is a DVR.
For each connected component of the generic torsor, use its stabilizer in G as the
Galois group. The ramification indices and residue degrees divide the stabilizer order
(Tag 09EB). They therefore divide the invertible order of G. The inseparable residue
extension has degree a power of the residue characteristic, so its degree is one.
Consequently the generic cover is tame in codimension one. Tag 0EYG gives an affine
etale neighbourhood of each point on which the punctured cover is a finite disjoint
union of standard root covers, all using the same equation for D. Tag 0EYH identifies
its normalization with the full standard root covers. Normalization commutes with
etale base change (03GE, 03GV), giving isomorphisms over each affine neighbourhood.
Finite disjoint unions of affine spectra are spectra of product rings. Enumerate the
finite component set by Fin m. Outside D split the finite etale cover etale locally and
use e = 1, f = 1. The empty family of
components gives m = 0 and the zero product ring. No section is required.
